summary.headline: Shivalik H1FY27: consolidated revenue up ~39%, EBITDA up 48%, PAT up 40%, driven by core components and value-add conversion.
summary.overview: Management said H1FY27 revenue grew about 39%, EBITDA 48% and PAT 40%, with growth led mainly by previously sampled core-component developments moving into regular business rather than by PCBA or CCS assemblies. Shunt volumes fell about 16% as customers shifted from wide strip to finished components, while value rose about 36% in shunts; management said commodity pass-through explains part of the value increase, with underlying volume-led growth of about 25-26%. Management outlined an assembly (busbar/PCBA) opportunity of INR 100-200 crore at a 15-16% EBITDA margin versus 26-27% for legacy lines, and a 3-4x revenue scale-up over a multi-year horizon with blended EBITDA moving toward 20-22%. No quantitative FY27 guidance was given; the call was mostly qualitative.

financial_highlights.change: YoY, of which 40-50% attributed to material (silver) prices
Per analyst question; management did not dispute

segments.name: Shunt resistors
segments.commentary: Volume down ~16% as strip sales to customers shifted to finished resistors; value up ~36%. US shipments declined as customer supply was redirected to end users mainly in Asia.

segments.name: Thermostatic bimetal
segments.commentary: India bimetal volumes rose sharply; management linked this to recovering switchgear and real-estate/infrastructure demand after a period of destocking. Outlook for medium and low voltage switchgear described as good for the next 2-3 quarters.

segments.name: Electrical contacts
segments.commentary: Revenue nearly doubled YoY, with 40-50% attributed to silver prices. New facility fully operational by July 2026; main core process for one product (~50% of contacts revenue) running at 50-60% utilisation; overall core processes ~55-60% by year-end.

segments.name: Busbar assemblies and PCBA/CCS
segments.commentary: Early-stage: one CCS customer in mass production with 2-3 programs in advanced stages. Opportunity sized at INR 100-200 crore at 15-16% EBITDA margin. To be reported as a separate fourth vertical; one vertical is a subsidiary (former JV).

guidance_outlook: FY27-FY28 illustrative case: 30-35% top-line growth sustainable over two years, with blended margin falling 1.5-2.5 percentage points on mix from 15-16% EBITDA assembly business; legacy lines margins expected to hold or improve.
Assembly opportunity of INR 100-200 crore; management stressed this is an opportunity, not assured business.
Over 3-4x today's revenue (roughly 3 years), mix could approach 50:50 between 26-27% and 15-16% EBITDA businesses, implying blended EBITDA of about 20-22%.
By end FY27-28, even INR 200-250 crore of PCBA business would be only 15-18% of total revenue.
Capex: heavy-capex areas have room; the INR 1,300 crore capacity number cited by analysts would be somewhat lower given earlier enhancements. New CFO joining by end-December 2026; COO search ongoing.
capex_capacity: Contacts: new facility fully functional by early July 2026; one core process ~50% of contacts revenue running at 50-60% utilisation; overall core utilisation expected ~55% by end FY27 (capacity originally INR 300-350 crore at half silver value, ~INR 400 crore at current silver).
Capex priorities: downstream processes at parts and assembly level (fast-cycle), end-of-line calibration and testing automation, and PCB/PCBA expansion.
Principal processes described as having sufficient capacity; downstream expansions added as order book requires.
Management said heavy-capex capacity has room; low-cost short-lead expansions will be added before over-utilisation.
demand_pricing: Growth driven mainly by core components: earlier sampling/pilot developments converted to regular business and a few large customers changed designs, with higher value-add per unit.
Silver roughly double YoY; around 64-65% of materials are pass-through, so commodity moves have minimal margin impact per management.
Management believes assembly business locks in for program life; component-level switching mid-cycle is rare in automotive.
Shunts for EV two-wheelers and ICE vehicles: 30-55 shunts per vehicle on lower-end cars; 200-250 on premium models.
Domestic EV/BMS/BESS demand is rising as battery pack assembly moves to India; BESS-related CCS/busbar work at early stage.
Inventory build attributed to development-stage programs with multiple validation cycles and busbar/PCBA needs; two to three programs underway to reduce inventory cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Is the current quarterly run-rate sustainable, and what is the demand outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said developments convert into sticky, staggered business; growth is expected to continue for a few years, though timing of new developments can be uneven.

qa_highlights.question: Why did shunt volume fall ~16% while value rose ~36%?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers previously bought wide strip for their own resistor production; that has dropped and SBCL now ships finished resistors with more processes. Commodity pass-through explains part of value growth; underlying volume-led growth is 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did US shunt revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Some US customers now receive supply directly for end users outside the US, mainly in Asia; some US demand resumed in the last 2-3 months, partly offset elsewhere.

qa_highlights.question: Will inorganic opportunities change capital allocation after the dividend?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend does not materially affect funds; free cash is sufficient, and acquisition opportunities are expected to come in staggered stages rather than requiring immediate capital.

qa_highlights.question: What is the assembly (busbar/PCBA) revenue potential and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Opportunity of INR 100-200 crore at 15-16% EBITDA versus 26-27% for legacy lines; will be shown as a separate fourth vertical; PCBA is seen as an extension of the shunt business, not a standalone core product.

qa_highlights.question: What is the contacts capacity utilisation and sustainable margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Core process for ~50% of contacts revenue at 50-60% utilisation; overall ~55% by end-year. Management said silver moves have limited margin impact because most profit comes from manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned and what is the capacity outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex on downstream processes, end-of-line testing automation and PCB/PCBA expansion; the INR 1,300 crore capacity figure would likely be somewhat lower given earlier enhancements.

risks_watch: Revenue timing depends on customer development cycles; management acknowledged possible ups and downs.
Margin dilution from 15-16% EBITDA assembly business; management guided 1.5-2.5 pp blended margin decline in the scenario discussed.
Inventory build-up and elevated working capital; management targets cash conversion improvement.
Silver and copper price volatility; management says impact is limited but contacts revenue is sensitive to large silver moves.
Key-person dependence on Kabir Ghumman; COO and new CFO hires are pending (CFO expected by end-December 2026).
Undisclosed new product areas in specialised electronic metals; timing of announcement said to be 'very soon'.
US-to-Asia rerouting of shunt shipments may distort geographic reporting.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core-component growth and margin trajectory, but cautious and hedged on timing of new assembly and CCS business ("a lot of ifs and buts"). Several answers were lengthy and some questions were deflected to later disclosure, notably on new product areas and FY27/28 specifics.
key_quotes: Consolidated revenue grew by approximately 39%, while EBITDA increased 48%, and profit rose, profit after tax rose 40%.
So what we look forward to now is at least a few more quarters of, you know, such value-added kind of growth, which is exactly the kind of growth that we like as a company.
We do not foresee, or we do not look at any of our PCBA assemblies, PCBA business, or PCB assembly businesses, or as becoming a core product of ours.
If we can add better value by going forward, and as well as, you know, get more business as a result, then why not?

adds.what: Contacts business new facility (fully operational by early July 2026)
Downstream parts/assembly processes, end-of-line calibration and testing automation, and PCB/PCBA expansion (fast-cycle, added as order book requires)

growth.why: Management gave no quantitative FY27 guidance; the illustrative FY27-28 case is 30-35% top-line growth sustained over two years, backed partly by a INR 100-200 crore assembly opportunity (explicitly 'an opportunity, not assured') and contacts utilisation rising to ~55% by year-end, with growth so far driven mainly by converted core-component developments and silver pass-through.

mgmt.note: New CFO joins by end-December 2026 and COO search is ongoing; no stated growth plan from the incoming executives.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided blended EBITDA down 1.5-2.5 pp as the 15-16% margin assembly business ramps, against 26-27% on legacy lines; the path to 20-22% blended margin is a 3-4 year story.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Contacts new facility already commissioned (July 2026), but downstream parts/assembly, end-of-line testing and PCB/PCBA expansion are planned as fast-cycle adds, with contacts core utilisation rising from 50-60% to ~55% overall by year-end.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Underlying volume-led shunt growth is ~25-26% ex-commodity, thermostatic bimetal volumes are rising with switchgear demand seen good for 2-3 quarters, and EV/BMS/BESS demand is rising, though shunt kg volumes fell ~16%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only ~55% overall, so no large announcement is forced, but management said low-cost short-lead expansions will be added as the INR 100-200 crore assembly order book requires and a 'some CAPEX' programme is ongoing.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1FY27 revenue grew ~39% and EBITDA ~48%, and the illustrative case is 30-35% top-line growth for two years, but the company has not issued numeric guidance to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged uneven timing of customer developments and a 1.5-2.5 pp blended EBITDA margin dip as the 15-16% assembly business scales, with no quantitative FY27 guidance given to measure against.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said an undisclosed new product area in specialised electronic metals will be announced 'very soon', and the CCS programme has 2-3 advanced-stage programs with one already in mass production.

rows.label: Assembly/busbar/PCBA opportunity INR 100-200 cr
rows.why: Opportunity sized at INR 100-200 crore at 15-16% EBITDA, with one CCS customer in mass production and 2-3 programs in advanced stages, but management stressed it is 'an opportunity, not assured'.

rows.label: Domestic EV/BMS/BESS demand shift
rows.why: Battery pack assembly is moving to India and BESS-related CCS/busbar work is at an early stage, supporting the assembly ramp.

rows.label: New CFO and COO hires
rows.why: New CFO is expected to join by end-December 2026 and COO search is ongoing, which matters given key-person dependence on Kabir Ghumman.

tone.note: Management was confident on core-component growth, silver pass-through and the 30-35% growth trajectory, but hedged and cautious on timing of the assembly and CCS business and deflected some questions on new product areas.
